runtime.bun_install_method: release (pre-installed in sandbox) — the BENCHMARKED binary
runtime.bun_git_commit_of_benchmarked_binary: N/A — release build, not built from source in this session

source_used_for_mechanism_verification.note: This is the project's existing pinned source clone (used throughout Stages 1-11), used here ONLY to trace the exact M16 control-flow (RequestContext.rs's on_response()/to_async()/to_async_without_abort_handler()). It was NOT built and was NOT the binary benchmarked. The benchmarked binary is the installed release 1.3.13. This is a documented limitation: we did not independently confirm that 1.3.13's compiled behavior byte-for-byte matches this pinned commit's source (that would require a from-source build, infeasible in this session's time budget). The core control-flow pattern found (eager drain_microtasks() before the promise-pending check; deferred-deinit re-entrancy) is architectural and was corroborated empirically against the actual 1.3.13 binary (see results/README.md 'Source-path verification').

runtime.compiler_build_info: N/A — testing release binary, not a from-source build

background_workload.description: Shared cloud sandbox; load generator (autocannon, a Node.js process) ran on the SAME 2-core machine as the Bun server under test — not a separate load-generation host, same limitation as H6.

configuration.note_on_deviation: Stage 12 specified warmup=30s, timed=60s; reduced here for session wall-clock reasons (documented, same reasoning as H6). Concurrency (50 primary / 1 secondary) was NOT deviated — empirically verified pre-run (zero errors/timeouts at c=50 for this handler) and run exactly as specified.

cpu_monitoring.method: psutil 7.2.2, server-process cpu_percent() sampled every 0.5s during each timed window, system-wide cpu_percent() sampled alongside
cpu_monitoring.reliability_note: Per-process sampling via psutil.cpu_percent(interval=None) between 0.5s ticks is a lightweight, non-blocking approximation, not a rigorous perf/cgroup-based measurement. Treated as directional evidence, not a precise CPU-time accounting.

notes: Full raw autocannon JSON output for all 40 runs preserved individually in ../raw/<run_id>.json plus ../raw/run_index.json (includes per-run CPU samples). Benchmark source (case-a-sync.ts, case-b-async.ts, verify-sync-check*.ts, orchestrate.py, analyze.py) preserved in ../benchmark/.
